name: Learning Loop Deck
description: A presentation skill for explaining a learning cycle or reporting a training pilot. It turns source material into action-titled 16:9 slides with a consistent four-stage loop, bright editorial typography, learner activities, and clearly labeled evidence.
whatYouGet: Action titles and varied slide layouts
Clear labeling for measured, proposed, and illustrative claims
goodFit: Explaining a new learning approach to facilitators
Reporting a training pilot to program sponsors
Turning a curriculum outline into a workshop briefing
notFor: Decks requiring an established brand template
requiredInputs: Evidence and its source, if available

faq.q: Can I use it without pilot results?
faq.a: Yes. The deck can explain a proposed learning cycle, but it will label goals and example figures as proposed or illustrative rather than measured outcomes.
Yes. Provide required terms and definitions. The loop labels can be adapted while their order and visual treatment stay consistent.

demoPrompt: /sl-learning-loop-deck Create exactly 9 slides for the fictional Regional Training Office: a four-week onboarding pilot for new service coordinators, moving from the learning gap through the practice-feedback loop and illustrative results to a scale decision. Title: “A shorter learning loop can make onboarding practice stick.” Close: “Approve a small pilot and review the evidence before scaling.” Use the Loop in Motion style.
followUpPrompts: Replace the illustrative numbers with these measured results and add the cohort definition.
Adapt the deck for a 20-minute facilitator briefing with one practice activity.
externalCostNote: No external services. Runs entirely on your agent.
